note: `defoverridable name: arity` is Elixir's override construct and the ONLY one the language has: it marks a published definition as an extension point and a LATER definition of the same name/arity replaces it, reaching the previous one through `super/1`. The edge shape is the bash lane's BD8b and for the same reason — Elixir has no classes and no superclass, so both endpoints name the same function and the LINES distinguish the versions: `overridesLine` is the declaration being replaced, `line_number` is the replacement. `never_replaced/0` is not in the `defoverridable` list and must produce nothing.
